newsitem.title: UK: Thorn dips further, analysts cautious.
newsitem.headline: Thorn dips further, analysts cautious.

text.p: Shares in Thorn Plc continued to slide on Monday, after the company's first half results earlier today were accompanied by a cautious trading outlook and as some analysts prepared to shave earnings forecasts.
The shares lost 24p to 323-1/2p by 1213 GMT.
Rodney Forest, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing said after returning from the analysts meeting, he would probably be cutting his full year and next year's interim forecasts.
"The comments about future trading were cautious," he said. "There was no clarification of the exposure to litigation, and the currency impact will probably hit more next year."
Forest had been expecting profits of 192 million stg for the current year and 212 million stg for the following year, towards the top of the range of expectations.
He added that next year's forecasts would probably bear the brunt of any downgrades.
Elsewhere, Morgan Stanley analyst Victoria Melendez expected to leave her forecasts unchanged following the meeting.
"I'm suprised that the shares are down 19p because while the company was cautious, it was certainly not a bearish meeting," she said.

She maintains forecasts of 189.2 million stg for the current year and 210.9 million stg pretax profit for 1997/98. "The key issue at Thorn is the return on sales," Melendez said. "In the UK this may be down at the final stage but should improve next year, and in the U.S. an improvement is expected after a fall this year, whilst in Europe exchange risks are likely to hit next year."
Melendez added that the outlook for net interest expense had also improved, and was now seen flat to lower in the coming year.
